p: — In the Midrash Rabbah on this parashah:
— Rabbi Akiva was sitting and expounding,
שֶׁתִּמְלֹךְ עַל מֵאָה עֶשְׂרִים וָשֶׁבַע מְדִינָה
— that she should reign over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces?
— who is the daughter of the daughter of Sarah,
,,, — who lived a hundred and twenty and seven years,” etc.
— why he came to rouse the congregation
— to such lofty words of Torah,
— in the manner of what is said:
— "Wisdom is too lofty for a fool," etc.
— And he wished to rouse them,
— is connected even to the lofty words of Torah,
— as they said in Tanna Devei Eliyahu
כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּב לוֹמַר
— “Each and every Jew is obligated to say,
, — the deeds of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov?’”
— since he is of the seed of the Patriarchs,
— has it in his power to reach,
— and in the manner of what they said
, — that does not have in it one like Avraham,” etc.

h: What Esther "saw": clothed in ruach hakodesh

p: — And this is what he said:
— “What did Esther see that she should reign,” etc.
— “By what merit did Esther come to reign,” etc.;
— is it then dependent on her?
— It seems that the intent is
— it should have said "royal garments," etc.;
— this teaches that ruach hakodesh clothed her:
— it is written here "and she clothed herself,"
— and it is written there, "And the spirit clothed Amasai."
— there it states explicitly "the spirit clothed,"
— where it is written, "Esther clothed herself in royalty";
— so how did he learn the one from the other?
— from the fact that it does not say "royal garments,"

paragraphs.text: Megillah 14b (end of the amud, running into 15a in the printed layout; Rav Tzadok cites "15a"): "Esther — as it is written, 'And it came to pass on the third day that Esther put on royalty': it should have said 'royal garments'! Rather, ruach hakodesh clothed her. It is written here 'put on,' and it is written there, 'and the spirit clothed Amasai.'" Rav Tzadok asks how the gezeirah shavah works when only Amasai's verse names the spirit, and answers that the derivation comes from the missing word "garments."

h: Malchut, ruach hakodesh, and the Oral Torah

p: — And this is the attribute of Malchut —
— of those who possess ruach hakodesh,
, — was a chariot for the attribute of Malchut;
— and in the Midrash Rabbah on this parashah:
— that he was the head of kingship
— And so it is brought from the Arizal
, — is the root of the Oral Torah.
— And this is what they said in the Midrash (Parashat Chukat):
— “Things that were not revealed to Moshe
— were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues;
— "and his eye has seen every precious thing"
, — this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues.”
— is the root of the Written Torah,
— as stated in the holy Zohar
— is from the attribute of Malchut,
— as the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote
עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב עַמּוּד א)
— "And a sage is greater than a prophet," etc.,
, — that it is through the attainment of ruach hakodesh.
— And although this is from the attribute of Malchut —
, — "the Supernal Crown is the crown of Malchut," etc.
— and this is "every precious thing," etc.,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִלָּה טז עַמּוּד ב)
— in the manner of what they said (Megillah 16b):
— which point to the Supernal Crown (Keter Elyon).
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
— because he is the root of the Oral Torah,

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 183a–b (Chukas): "Rabbi Yitzchak began: 'And it came to pass on the third day, and Esther put on royalty' (Esther 5:1). The Scroll of Esther was said with ruach hakodesh, and therefore it is written among the Writings... 'And Esther put on royalty' — what is 'royalty'? If you say garments of honor and purple, that is not what it is called; rather, 'Esther put on royalty', for she was clothed in the supernal holy Malchus; she certainly put on ruach hakodesh. Why did she merit this place? Because she guarded her mouth and did not tell anything, as it is written, 'Esther did not tell her kindred' (Esther 2:20)." This is the unstated source for Rav Tzadok's equation of Malchus with ruach hakodesh; compare Zohar III 275b (Ki Teitzei): "she merited to be clothed in ruach hakodesh, as it is written, 'And Esther put on royalty'."

h: Sarah's years, all counted for good

p: — And this is what is written:
— and to rely on a miracle?
— who is the daughter of the daughter of Sarah,
— who lived a hundred and twenty-seven years,
— and all the days of her life were included for good:
— at a hundred like at twenty;
— as they said in the Midrash Rabbah:
— in which there is no understanding,
— who was born of the seed of Terach.
— And regarding Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
— only that God, blessed be He, assured him
— that he need not grieve over them (those earlier years),
— Sarah too was not at first

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 58:1, on Tehillim 37:18: "Just as they are whole, so their years are whole: at twenty like at seven for beauty, at a hundred like at twenty as to sin." Rav Tzadok extends "whole" to the years before understanding. The print's "shechitah" ("slaughter," in "shechitah 127 years") is corrected to "she-chaysah" ("who lived").

paragraphs.text: Parallels: Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah 3 — the same midrash: the years are "whole" because even the years of childhood are counted, joined to Bereishis Rabbah 39:8. · Chiddushei HaRim, Chayei Sarah 1 (Chassidus) — on Rashi's "all of them were equal in goodness": not repentance that recasts earlier years, but that she never sinned. This is a contrast to Rav Tzadok, who allows that Sarah "was not at first as afterward."

h: From Sarah to Esther to every Jew

p: — From this Esther clothed herself in royalty,
— since God, blessed be He, had arranged for her
— the rescue of all Israel through her.
— And from this she put on royalty,
— and she would not fear at all.
— And this is why Rabbi Akiva came
— that a person should not say,
— “What am I and what is my life,
— and what connection do I have
— to the lofty words of Torah,”
, — when he knows the plagues of his own heart.
וְעַל זֶה בָּא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְעוֹרֵר
— And about this Rabbi Akiva came to rouse them:
— just as Esther learned from Sarah.
— that just as every single Jew
— the deeds of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov,”
— they planted in the heart of their offspring
— that each and every Jew would be able
— to be helped by the service of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs
— when he comes to purify himself.
— even in the lofty words of Torah,
